claims.text: Reducing the SPS consolidation temperature of ZrB2–AlFeNiCoCr cermets reduces the formation of harmful intermetallic phases.
Reducing the SPS consolidation temperature of ZrB2–AlFeNiCoCr cermets reduces microstructural segregation.
Lower-temperature SPS improves molten-aluminum corrosion resistance relative to conventional higher-temperature SPS.
Lower-temperature SPS produces a refined microstructure.
Lower sintering temperatures limit reactions between ZrB2 and the AlFeNiCoCr alloy constituents.
Reduced reaction between ZrB2 and the alloy constituents suppresses intermetallic-phase formation.
The intermetallic phases formed during higher-temperature processing compromise the corrosion-resistant boride matrix.
Reduced intermetallic content and segregation enhance resistance to degradation in molten aluminum.
Low-temperature-SPS samples will exhibit a lower molten-aluminum corrosion rate than high-temperature-SPS samples.
Low-temperature-SPS samples will exhibit reduced molten-aluminum penetration depth.
Lower-temperature SPS will increase component service lifetime relative to conventional higher-temperature SPS.
The corrosion benefit should persist under standard hot-dip aluminum-plating temperatures and molten-aluminum exposure conditions.
The intervention may cease to be beneficial if the lower SPS temperature compromises densification.
Lower-temperature SPS may create mechanical-property deficits that offset its anticipated benefit.
